tools.name: delete_folder
tools.description: Delete one of the account's own folders and everything nested under it. This removes the folder structure only; the media and entities inside are pointers, so the underlying assets are never deleted. Confirm intent before deleting a folder that contains items.

tools.name: get_media
tools.description: SEE specific media, up to 5 items. This is for YOUR eyes only: it returns image blocks so you can judge a face, check legibility or compare variations, and it renders NOTHING for the person. If they should see it, call show_media, which displays up to 100 items and costs you almost no context. Pass a batch of items to view at once, returned as image blocks for you: each item is either a { url } (e.g. a URL threaded from view, a layer/asset URL from get_project / get_card, or an upload URL from list_media source=uploads) or a { mediaId } (the media id list_media, search_media and get_folder print: a1B2c3D4, or a1B2c3D4-2 for one output of a generation with several). Returns light metadata per item plus an IMAGE block for each image so you can actually see it. To see a clip's frames, use view; audio still returns metadata + the url, and the metadata of an audio item names its size, duration and container with the stream facts the file states (its codec, sample rate and channels), each only when known. A bare id for a generation returns ONLY its primary output, named by its full media id, and lists the others' media ids; pass one of those to see it. To ZOOM into an image, set region { x, y, width, height } on an item, in the image's own pixels: that part is cut from the original and returned at its own detail, never enlarged, so you can check small text or an edge. Use this to inspect the actual pixels, not just URLs.

items.description: The media to LOOK at, up to 5 per call. Five is where the inline byte budget runs out, not a round number. Use show_media for a larger set you only need to display.

region.description: Zoom: the part of an image to cut out, in its own pixels (an item's geometry gives its size). Cut from the original and returned at its own detail, never enlarged; clamped to the file.

url.description: A media URL on our storage (from view / get_project / get_card).

mediaId.description: A media id as list_media, search_media and get_folder print it (a1B2c3D4, or a1B2c3D4-2 for one output of several).

region.description: Zoom: the part of an image to cut out, in its own pixels (an item's geometry gives its size). Cut from the original and returned at its own detail, never enlarged; clamped to the file.

tools.name: update_media
tools.description: Rename a stored file or give it a description, after upload. Pass name, description or both; passing neither is refused. Only files in the library can be changed this way: a generated output or a stock item cannot. An empty description clears it. Returns the file as get_media reads it, with its new name and description. Requires the library:write scope.

description.description: A description of the file, in your own words.

mediaId.description: The file's media id, as list_media, search_media and get_folder print it.

name.description: The new name for the file.

tools.name: show_media
tools.description: SHOW media to the person, up to 100 items in one card. Use this to present a set you do not need to look at yourself: search results, a folder, a shortlist, everything a list_media call returned. It renders a grid the person can browse, expand and act on, and it costs you almost no context because it returns urls rather than pixels. Each item is a { url } or a { mediaId }, the same shapes get_media takes. Pair it with list_media: list to FIND, show to PRESENT. Do not re-show media another tool already displayed: anything that creates or imports media renders its own card, and showing it again only duplicates it. If you need to SEE the pixels yourself (judge a face, check legibility, compare variations) use get_media instead, which attaches image blocks for up to 5 items.

items.description: The media to show, up to 100 items per call.

url.description: A media URL on one of our storage hosts.

mediaId.description: A media id as list_media, search_media and get_folder print it (a1B2c3D4, or a1B2c3D4-2 for one output of several).

tools.name: create_upload
tools.description: Begin uploading local files as library media. Takes each file's name, type and size in bytes, and answers for each an upload target, which is a temporary write permission and not a media address. A single target: PUT the whole file to its url with exactly its headers. A multipart target: the file goes in parts of the size it states, each signed with sign_upload_parts; PUT each part to its url and keep the ETag header of the store's answer. Then call complete_upload once for the batch. The finished media is referenced by its outputId in generate_* and on a card via update_card. For a file already at a public address, use import. Requires the library:write scope.

contentType.description: The MIME type of the file.

fileName.description: The file name, used for its extension.

sizeBytes.description: The size of the file in bytes. The store chooses how the file is uploaded from it.

tools.name: sign_upload_parts
tools.description: Sign parts of a multipart upload. Takes the outputId create_upload answered and the numbers of the parts to send, counted from 1. Answers a url and headers for each: PUT that part's bytes to its url with exactly those headers and keep the ETag header of the store's answer. Part n starts at (n - 1) times the part size create_upload stated and is that long, the last part ending where the file ends. Signed when asked and safe to ask again, so a slow or interrupted upload asks only for the parts it still needs. Requires the library:write scope.

outputId.description: The outputId create_upload answered for the file.

partNumbers.description: The numbers of the parts to sign, counted from 1.

tools.name: complete_upload
tools.description: Finish uploads once their bytes were sent. Takes each file's outputId and, for a multipart file, the number and ETag of every part, exactly as the store answered. Finish a batch together, so the person sees it as one card. Publishes each file and answers its outputId and URL. Finishing twice answers the same media. Requires the library:write scope.

outputId.description: The outputId create_upload answered for the file.

parts.description: Multipart files only: the number and ETag of every part, exactly as the store answered its PUT.

etag.description: The ETag header of the store's answer to the part's PUT, exactly as received.

tools.name: import
tools.description: Bring something into your own library or a new project. Pass exactly one source, and what comes back follows it. url: a file address (an image, video or audio file) becomes library media, free; a video page address on a supported site becomes library media too, and spends credits: the most its download may cost is held and it is charged for what arrived. pptxUrl (a PowerPoint or Google Slides file) or canvaDesignId (a Canva design, through the account's Canva connection) becomes a new canvas project with editable layers, free; cardId links it to its card in the same call. Pass getCost to see what an import would spend first: nothing runs and nothing is charged. Imported media is referenced by its outputId in generate_* and on a card via update_card. A media import still running at the end of the call returns pending: wait for it with get_status. A tracked post's video is not imported: analyze_content with kind video downloads it for analysis. Scopes: library:write for a url, editor:write for a project (and planner:write with cardId).

canvaDesignId.description: A Canva design id: imported into a new canvas project through the account's Canva connection (fails with canva_not_connected when it is not linked).

cardId.description: With pptxUrl or canvaDesignId: the card this project is for. The new project is linked to it in the same call (it shows among the card's assets), so the card opens the edit from the moment it exists. Also needs the planner:write scope.

contentType.description: With url: a MIME override (else taken from the response).

fileName.description: With url: a file name (used for its extension).

getCost.description: Return what this import would spend instead of importing (nothing runs, nothing is charged). 0 for a file address or a project.

pptxUrl.description: A PowerPoint or Google Slides file address: imported into a new canvas project.

title.description: With pptxUrl or canvaDesignId: the new project's title.

url.description: A public https address: a file, imported free into the library, or a video page on a supported site, whose video is downloaded into the library and spends.

tools.name: download
tools.description: Download any file of the account's out of ContentHero to keep: a generation (every output, or one output by its -<n> media id), an upload, an import, a library file, or a project's export, named by its media id or export id. Answers each file's name and a save link that names the file, needs no sign-in and does not expire: fetch the link for the file itself. Free: it reads what is already stored. A file not made yet is refused with the step that follows it.

id.description: A media id (a generation, -<n> for one of its outputs, an upload, an import, a library file) or an export id.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the generation models available to this account (the discovery catalog): which models exist, their content type and operation, and a compact capability summary. Use this to pick a model, then call get_model for its full request shape before generating. Source of truth for valid model ids; do not hardcode them.

tools.name: get_model
tools.description: Get one model's full request shape by id: the exact parameters it accepts (input types, prompt mode and char cap, duration range, resolutions, aspect ratios, max references, generation count, audio, features). Ground a generation against this instead of guessing the parameters, then preview cost with the matching generate tool's getCost option before running it.

modelId.description: The model id, as list_models names it.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Get a vocabulary another call accepts, by kind. 'platform': with no platform, the platforms this account can publish to, each with its formats and whether a connected account exists; with a platform (and optionally a format), the fields, options (enums) and character limits a post requires per format. Ground a post's platformSettings against it instead of guessing the fields. 'timeline': the EDITOR timeline schema, in two steps. Without a name, its index: every update_timeline op with its shape, every clip and track type, and the rules every op follows. With a name, that one entry in full: an op with its rules, or a clip type with its fields (each with who writes it, its range and its allowed values), the shared field groups it has and a copy-pasteable `example` clip; the name 'animations' reads the presets add_animation, add_transition and apply_combo take. detail 'full' reads the whole schema at once. Read the index, then the entries you need, before building any clip with update_timeline. 'layer': the CANVAS schema, in the same two steps. Without a name, its index: every update_canvas op with its shape, every layer type, and the rules every op follows. With a name, that one entry in full: an op with its rules, or a layer type with its fields and the shared field groups it has. detail 'full' reads the whole schema at once. Read the index, then the entries you need, before building any layer with update_canvas. 'export': the export formats and their options per project type, so you know what export accepts. 'link': the grammar of app addresses and every noun and section it takes (what each opens, its tabs, what a tab's item names) plus the app's origin, so you can build a link to any item from its noun and id. 'code': the authoring guide for a code clip or code layer (a video, audio or image whose content is code): what the sandbox can import and what it cannot use, the box the code draws in, the sound it can synthesize, the brand prop names, the size limit, the workflow and examples; read it before writing or changing a clip's code. 'effect': every effect code or a video or image clip can use, by group, with what it does, where code imports it, and whether a clip can carry it; with a name, that effect's parameters with their ranges and defaults, and which of them keyframe on a clip. Read it before giving anything effects. 'timeline', 'layer', 'export', 'code' and 'effect' require the editor:read scope.

detail.description: kinds 'timeline' and 'layer' only: 'full' reads the whole schema at once. It is large; read the index and the entries you need instead unless you need everything.

format.description: kind 'platform' with a platform only: a format to narrow to (e.g. "reel", "short", "story", "thread").

jsonSchema.description: kinds 'timeline' and 'layer' only, with a type's name or detail 'full': also return each type's full JSON Schema. It is large; ask for it only to validate a whole item before sending it.

name.description: kind 'effect': the effect to read in full (such as "glow"); omit to list the effects. kind 'timeline': one op or clip type to read in full, or 'animations' for the presets; omit for the index. kind 'layer': one op or layer type to read in full; omit for the index.

platform.description: kind 'platform' only: the platform to read (such as "instagram"). Omit to list every platform.

tools.name: list_kling_elements
tools.description: List the account's saved Kling elements. A Kling element is Kling 3.0's saved reference for one character, location or prop: 2-4 images (or one video) of it under a name, so the subject stays consistent across Kling video generations. Use one in generate_video's klingElements by klingElementId, and as @name in the prompt.

tools.name: get_kling_element
tools.description: Get one saved Kling element by id: its name, category, description, and images.

tools.name: create_kling_element
tools.description: Create a Kling element: a saved reference for one character, location or prop that keeps it consistent across Kling 3.0 video generations. Give it 2-4 images (or one video) of that one subject; images may be URLs or output-id tokens, so you can generate the angle shots first and assemble the Kling element from them. Use it later in generate_video's klingElements [{ klingElementId }] and as @name in the prompt.

video.description: A single video URL or output-id token (alternative to images).

tools.name: update_kling_element
tools.description: Update a saved Kling element's name, description, or category.

category.description: What kind of Kling element this is. 'auto' lets the server classify it from the image.

description.description: What this Kling element is, in words. This is what makes it findable later.

tools.name: delete_kling_element
tools.description: Permanently delete a saved Kling element. Videos already generated with it are unaffected.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Check any background job: generations and edits, exports, brand kit reads, avatars, a post's analysis or scenes, and transcripts. Pass the ids the calls that started them returned; an id alone names its job. Each id answers on its own line, so one that names no job of yours says why and the others still answer. Pass kind only for a full UUID, for scenes or a transcript (the id is the post or media it belongs to), or when the answer says an id is ambiguous. BY DEFAULT THIS BLOCKS until the jobs finish, up to ~40s per call, because that is almost always what you want after starting one; a job still running comes back with where it is and a poll_after_seconds hint, so call again. Pass wait:false for an instant snapshot with no blocking. A finished generation answers with its final URLs. A job is over only when its status is settled or failed. Processing and applying mean it is still running; keep reading the same id.

ids.description: The jobs to check, each by the id the call that started it returned.

kind.description: Which kind of job the ids name. Only for a full UUID, scenes, a transcript, or an id the answer says is ambiguous.

wait.description: Block until the jobs finish (up to ~40s), the default. false = an instant snapshot.

tools.name: list_cards
tools.description: List one SPACE's cards (newest-updated first). ⚠️ SCOPED, NOT COMPLETE: without spaceId this lists the account's DEFAULT space only, and cards on any other board are absent with nothing in the response saying so (search misses them too). Call list_spaces FIRST and pass spaceId unless you specifically mean the default board. Filter by status, platform, stage (id/slug/name), favorite, tag, or a title search. Call get_card for one card's full detail (posts + assets).

archived.description: Only ARCHIVED cards. Archived cards are excluded by default, matching the board.

search.description: Case-insensitive title search, scoped to the chosen space.

spaceId.description: Which space's board to list, from list_spaces, or 'all' for every space. Omit ONLY when you mean the account's default space; omitting it does not search every board.

stage.description: Filter by a stage id, slug, or name. Resolved within the chosen space. Needed for sort position, which reads that stage's own order.

tools.name: get_card
tools.description: Get one CARD in full: its fields (title, description, script, notes, status, stage, schedule), plus its posts (one per platform, which is how it publishes) and its attached assets in carousel order. An [inspiration] asset is a tracked post attached as a reference; its line already carries the headline metrics (creator, outlier score, views, likes, duration) plus transcript and breakdown availability, and a content id to pass to get_content for the transcript and the full Break It Down analysis. To attach one, add { contentId } to the assets list of update_card; a linked editor or canvas project is added the same way with { projectId }.

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: List the account's SPACES. A space is the planner's top-level container: Space > Stage > Card > Post. Each space has its own stages, so two spaces can both hold a stage called 'Published'. Call this FIRST to discover which board to work in, then pass a space id to list_stages, list_cards or create_card. Archived spaces are excluded unless archived is set, which lists only them.

archived.description: Only archived spaces. Archived spaces are excluded by default, matching the grid in the app.

tools.name: get_space
tools.description: Return one space with its live card count. Use list_spaces to discover ids. The count excludes archived cards, and is the same number list_spaces reports for that space.

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a space: a new planner board with its own stages. duplicateFrom copies another space's STAGES, never its cards, so the new board arrives with the columns and none of the work. Requires the planner:write scope.

coverUrl.description: A cover image URL for the space tile.

duplicateFrom.description: Copy this space's stages into the new one. Cards are never copied.

tools.name: update_space
tools.description: Rename a space or change its cover. This is a PATCH: a field you omit is left alone, so renaming does not disturb the cover. Pass coverUrl as an empty string to REMOVE the cover. To favorite or archive a space, use the `favorite` and `archive` tools with assetType 'space' instead. Requires the planner:write scope.

coverUrl.description: A new cover image URL. Pass an empty string to remove the cover entirely.

tools.name: delete_space
tools.description: Delete a space. The server REFUSES a space that still holds cards and names the count, because the delete cascades to every card in it along with their covers, captions, posts and schedules. Archive the space instead if you want it out of the way. Requires the planner:write scope.

tools.name: list_stages
tools.description: List one SPACE's stages, in order. ⚠️ STAGES ARE PER-SPACE: without spaceId this is the account's DEFAULT space, and two spaces can each hold a stage named 'Published' with different ids, so a stage name resolved against the wrong space is a different column. Stages are user-customizable (renamed, reordered, added, removed), so call this to discover the real stages before placing a card; pass a stage's id (most stable), slug, or name to create_card / update_card.

spaceId.description: Which space's stages, from list_spaces. Omit only when you mean the account's default space.

tools.name: create_stage
tools.description: Create a stage (a column on one board). ⚠️ STAGES ARE PER-SPACE: without spaceId this creates on the account's DEFAULT board, which is rarely what you want once more than one space exists, so call list_spaces first. The slug is DERIVED from the name and is not settable; a board cannot hold two columns whose names produce the same slug and the server refuses the second rather than renaming it for you. Place the column with afterId, beforeId or position (top is the first column), or name none to put it at the end. Requires the planner:write scope.

afterId.description: Place it immediately after this item of the same list.

beforeId.description: Place it immediately before this item of the same list.

name.description: The column name, for example "In Review". Must contain a letter or number.

position.description: Place it at an end of the list instead of beside an item. Name neighbors or a position, not both.

spaceId.description: Which board, from list_spaces. Omit only when you mean the account's default space.

tools.name: update_stage
tools.description: Rename, recolor or move one stage. This is a PATCH: a field you omit is left alone. ⚠️ spaceId is REQUIRED, because a stage id alone does not tell the server which board you mean and guessing the wrong one silently changes nothing. Renaming re-derives the slug, so renaming a column away from 'Published' also stops publishing auto-moving cards into it; a rename that collides with another column on the same board is refused. Moving names NEIGHBORS or an end, never a number: pass afterId, beforeId, or position (top is the first column). Requires the planner:write scope.

afterId.description: Place it immediately after this item of the same list.

beforeId.description: Place it immediately before this item of the same list.

color.description: A new hex color such as "#3B82F6".

name.description: A new name. The slug follows it automatically.

position.description: Place it at an end of the list instead of beside an item. Name neighbors or a position, not both.

spaceId.description: The board this stage is on, from list_stages or list_spaces.

stageId.description: The stage id to update, from list_stages.

tools.name: delete_stage
tools.description: Delete a stage and move its cards to another column. The server REFUSES a column that still holds cards when you name no targetStageId, and tells you how many there are: cards are never destroyed by deleting a column, and the delete and the reassignment happen in one transaction. Returns the board that is left. Requires the planner:write scope.

spaceId.description: The board this stage is on.

stageId.description: The stage id to delete, from list_stages.

targetStageId.description: Where this column's cards should go. Required unless the column is empty.

tools.name: create_card
tools.description: Create a card, the container in the content pipeline. A card holds the work (title, notes, cover) and the posts that publish it. Attach posts and media by passing `posts` and `assets` to update_card, then publish with publish_post. ⚠️ WITHOUT spaceId THIS LANDS ON THE ACCOUNT'S DEFAULT BOARD, which is rarely what you want once more than one space exists, so call list_spaces first. `stage` accepts a stage id/slug/name and DECIDES the space when it is an id; a spaceId that disagrees with it is rejected rather than guessed. Requires a key with the planner:write scope.

afterId.description: Place it immediately after this item of the same list.

beforeId.description: Place it immediately before this item of the same list.

contentType.description: What kind of content the card holds, in a word.

coverOutputId.description: A media token (short id, output id or first 8 characters, optionally with "-N") for the cover, resolved to its URL. Use this or coverUrl.

coverUrl.description: Public URL for the post cover (the card thumbnail).

position.description: Place it at an end of the list instead of beside an item. Name neighbors or a position, not both.

spaceId.description: Which board to create the card on, from list_spaces. Omit only when you mean the account's default space.

stage.description: Stage id, slug, or name. Defaults to the first stage.

tags.description: Tag names to set on the post (must already exist; see list_tags / create_tag). Replaces the set.

tools.name: update_card
tools.description: Update a card: its fields (title, notes, platform, cover, stage), its POSTS (one per platform, which is how it publishes), its ASSETS (its files, links, linked projects and inspiration posts, in order), and its SCHEDULE. posts and assets are DECLARATIVE: pass the WHOLE set, because anything you leave out is removed. Posts key on platform. Assets key on id, and THE ARRAY ORDER IS THE carousel ORDER, so reordering is just sending the same ids in a different order; keep an existing asset by id, and add a new one by EXACTLY ONE reference: outputId (media: a generation, an upload or an import), assetUrl (a link), contentId (an inspiration post, shown on the card's Inspiration tab) or projectId (an editor or canvas project); get_card reads each back under the same field name. Listing the same thing twice is refused. To attach one thing, read the card, append the entry to its assets, and send the whole list back. scheduledAt sets the time on the card AND every post (pass null to clear); give a post its own scheduledAt to override it for that platform. To publish NOW, use publish_post. Pass spaceId to MOVE the card to another space; without a stage it lands in the target space's stage whose slug matches its current one, or that space's first stage. Pass cardIds to update several cards at once, which crossed with spaceId is how a selection moves in one call; fields that describe ONE card (title, notes, cover) still need exactly one. WRITING notes REQUIRES expectedRevision: read the card first and pass the revision it reported, or the call is refused. Requires the planner:write scope.

afterId.description: Place it immediately after this item of the same list.

assets.description: The post's assets IN ORDER, each { id } to keep an existing one or ONE of { outputId } | { assetUrl, assetType? } | { contentId } | { projectId } to add. REPLACES the list; [] clears it.

assetType.description: Accepted and not needed: the kind is read from what the entry points at. Never 'inspiration' or a project type: use contentId or projectId.

assetUrl.description: ADD a link by its url. Nothing is copied; to keep a copy of a file on the web, import it and add the outputId.

contentId.description: ADD an inspiration post, by its id or short id, its link, or the platform's own id for it. It lands on the card's Inspiration tab.

id.description: Keep an existing asset, at this position in the order.

outputId.description: ADD media in ContentHero by its output id: a generation, a file uploaded from a device (create_upload then complete_upload), or a file imported from a url (import). "<id>-2" is variation 2 of a batch.

projectId.description: ADD a link to an editor or canvas project: its project id.

beforeId.description: Place it immediately before this item of the same list.

cardIds.description: Update several cards at once. Fields that describe ONE card (title, notes, cover) still require exactly one.

contentType.description: What kind of content the card holds, in a word. An empty string clears it.

coverOutputId.description: A media token (short id, output id or first 8 characters, optionally with "-N") for the cover, resolved to its URL.

coverUrl.description: Public URL for the post cover.

expectedRevision.description: REQUIRED when writing notes: the revision get_card reported for this card. A card's notes have four independent writers, each reading the whole document and writing it back, so without this the last writer silently erases the others and still gets a success. If the card changed since you read it, the call fails with a conflict carrying the current notes and revision: merge onto those and retry with the revision they came with. Never guess it or add one to it, because it only advances when notes actually change.

notes.description: Working notes on the card. Plain text or markdown; tables render here. No emojis.

notesEdits.description: Change the notes in place without resending them. Each edit is { append: text }, which adds to the end, or { find, replace }, where find must match exactly one place in the current notes. Edits apply in order, all or none, to the notes as they are when the call arrives, so no expectedRevision is needed. Prefer this to notes for any change smaller than a rewrite.

platform.description: The card's primary platform. This is a label on the card; what actually publishes is its posts.

position.description: Place it at an end of the list instead of beside an item. Name neighbors or a position, not both.

posts.description: The card's posts, each { platform, format?, connectedAccountId?, platformSpecificData?, scheduledAt?, status? }. REPLACES the set, keyed by platform; [] detaches all.

platform.description: The platform. This is the KEY: one post per platform.

platformSpecificData.description: The publish payload for this platform.

scheduledAt.description: Per-post override of the card's schedule.
ISO time to publish. Sets the card AND every post. null clears the schedule.

spaceId.description: Move the card to a different space (id or slug). Without a stage, it lands in that space's stage whose slug matches its current one, or that space's first stage.

stage.description: Move the card to this stage (id, slug, or name).

tags.description: Tag names to set on the post (must already exist; replaces the set). Omit to leave tags unchanged.

title.description: Rename the card. Keep it short: a long title wraps and makes the column unreadable.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: List the account's tags (the organizational tag library). Set a post's tags with the `tags` field on create_card / update_card. A tag is just a lowercase name.

tools.name: create_tag
tools.description: Create a tag in the account's tag library (the name is lowercased). Tags organize posts; apply them with the `tags` field on create_card / update_card. Requires the planner:write scope.

tools.name: update_tag
tools.description: Rename a tag (preserves its assignments on all posts). To detach a tag from one post, set that post's `tags` without it via update_card. Requires the planner:write scope.

name.description: The new tag name (lowercased on save).

tools.name: delete_tag
tools.description: Delete a tag from the account's library. This DESTROYS the tag and removes it from every post it was on. To just detach a tag from one post, set that post's `tags` without it via update_card instead. Requires the planner:write scope.

tools.name: publish_post
tools.description: Publish a card's posts NOW: every post on the card, or only the named platform's post when `platform` is given. Each post must have a connected account. Requires a key with the publish:write scope; holding that scope is the account owner's consent to autonomous publishing. Returns one result per post.

platform.description: Publish only this platform. Omit to publish all posts.

tools.name: list_tracked_accounts
tools.description: List the social accounts this ContentHero account tracks. TWO KINDS, in one list: accountType 'inspiration' is the creators and competitors they watch for research, 'brand' is their OWN profiles (distinct from list_brand_kits, which are the brand identity documents). Every row reports its own accountType, so omit the filter to see both. Call get_tracked_account for one account's performance, or list_content for the posts. Pass brandKitId to scope to the accounts linked to a specific brand kit.

accountType.description: Narrow to one kind. Omitted, both come back.

brandKitId.description: Scope to the accounts linked to this brand kit (from get_brand_kit).

tools.name: get_tracked_account
tools.description: Get one tracked account with how its content actually performs: post count, total and average views/likes/comments, average engagement and outlier score, plus its top posts by outlier score and its most recent ones. Works for either kind of account: use it on one of the owner's OWN accounts to ground decisions in their real numbers, or on a creator they watch to study what works for that creator.

accountId.description: One of your tracked accounts: its id or short id, its profile link, its handle, or the platform's own id for it.

tools.name: update_tracked_account
tools.description: Move a tracked account within its list (its kind's: the creators they watch, or their own profiles), after or before another of the same kind, or to an end. Returns the account with its performance, as get_tracked_account does. Requires the inspiration:write scope.

accountId.description: One of your tracked accounts: its id or short id, its profile link, its handle, or the platform's own id for it.

afterId.description: Place it immediately after this item of the same list.

beforeId.description: Place it immediately before this item of the same list.

position.description: Place it at an end of the list instead of beside an item. Name neighbors or a position, not both.

tools.name: add_tracked_account
tools.description: Track social accounts by handle or profile URL. accountType 'inspiration' (the default) is the creators the user watches, 'brand' is their own profiles. Inspiration accounts count toward the plan's limit: accounts past it are not tracked and come back as not tracked, with the refusal. Each tracked account comes back with its outcome: added, restored or already tracked. Its posts arrive once it syncs. Requires the inspiration:write scope.

accountType.description: Which list they join: inspiration (the default) or brand.

accounts.description: The accounts to track, in the order they are listed.

handleOrUrl.description: A handle or a profile URL.

platform.description: The platform. Needed for a bare handle; a profile URL states its own.

brandKitId.description: Also link each account to this brand kit (from list_brand_kits).

tools.name: remove_tracked_account
tools.description: Stop tracking a social account. Its posts and analyses are kept, and adding it again restores it. Requires the inspiration:write scope.

accountId.description: One of your tracked accounts: its id or short id, its profile link, its handle, or the platform's own id for it.

tools.name: list_content
tools.description: The core research read: social posts this account tracks, ranked by OUTLIER SCORE (how far a post overperformed its own creator's baseline, so a small account's hit still surfaces), or by relevance when you pass search. SPANS BOTH the creators they watch and their OWN posts by default; set scope to narrow. This is how you answer both "what is working for the people I watch" and "how did my own posts do" without picking a subsystem first. Filter by platform, content type, a published window (publicationDate like 'week' or 'month', or exact publishedAfter/publishedBefore), and ranges over score, views, duration and follower count. Call get_content for one post in full, including its transcript.

accountIds.description: Limit to these tracked accounts, each by its id or short id, its profile link, its handle, or the platform's own id for it.

addedByYou.description: Only the one-off posts the owner saved by url.

brandKitId.description: Scope to the accounts linked to this brand kit.

favorited.description: Only content the account has favorited.

outlierScoreMax.description: Only content at or below this outlier score.

outlierScoreMin.description: Only content at or above this outlier score.

publicationDate.description: Published within this window. Use publishedAfter for an exact date instead.

scope.description: 'inspiration' = creators they watch, 'brand' = their own accounts, 'all' = both (default).

search.description: Finds posts by meaning and by keyword across title, creator, description and transcript, ranked by relevance, or the one post a pasted link names. Returns only the posts judged relevant, never the unranked candidates. An empty result carries emptyReason: nothing matched, the relevance judge was unavailable (try again), or the link names no post this list covers.

subscribersMax.description: Maximum follower count of the post's account.

subscribersMin.description: Minimum follower count of the post's account.

viewsMax.description: Only content at or below this view count.

viewsMin.description: Only content at or above this view count.

tools.name: get_content
tools.description: Get one tracked post in full: engagement stats, outlier score, hashtags, keywords, mentions and audio info. Works for a creator's post and for the owner's own. THE TRANSCRIPT IS OPT-IN because a long video is a large document: pass transcript='text' for the whole thing, or transcript='segments' for timed slices, and then narrow with startMs/endMs or transcriptSearch to pull only the part that matters. The transcript reports a status: 'complete', 'not_applicable' (there is nothing to transcribe), 'failed' (it will be retried), 'processing', or 'absent' (never attempted), so an empty result is never ambiguous. THE BREAK IT DOWN ANALYSIS IS OPT-IN THE SAME WAY: availability (status + section names) is always reported; pass analysis='full' for every section, or analysisSections for only the ones the task needs. SCENES ARE OPT-IN THE SAME WAY: availability is always reported; pass scenes='map' for each scene's time range, what happens in it and what is said. Scenes are descriptions only: see a scene's frames with view, by contentId and atSec in its range. startMs/endMs narrow either. Scenes exist once analyze_content has run with kind scenes. Each of the post's videos is reported with its state; once analyze_content kind video has downloaded one, cuts adds where its picture changes. Each video also reports its audio map summary (speech, sound candidates, music, loudness), free; audioMap adds the map for the window. transcriptSegments is excluded from 'full' because the transcript params above are the one transcript path.

analysis.description: How much of the post's Break It Down analysis to include. Default 'none' (availability + section names still report).

analysisSections.description: Only these analysis sections. The names differ by format, so take them from the availability line.

audioMap.description: Add each video's audio map window: speech, sound candidates with their measured descriptors, music, loudness and each stem's level, measured once and free. Each video's summary reports either way. startMs and endMs narrow the window.

contentId.description: The post: its id or short id, its link, or the platform's own id for it.

cuts.description: Add each downloaded video's cut list: the seconds where its picture changes, measured once and free. startMs and endMs narrow the lists.

endMs.description: Window end, ms from the start of the media. Narrows transcript segments, scenes and cut lists.

scenes.description: How much of the post's scene map to include. Default 'none' (availability still reports). 'map' adds each scene's range, what happens and what is said; view shows its frames.

startMs.description: Window start, ms from the start of the media. Narrows transcript segments, scenes and cut lists.

transcript.description: How much transcript to include. Default 'none'. 'words' adds each word's start and end to the segments, where the post has word timing.

transcriptSearch.description: Return only the segments containing this phrase. Implies segments.

tools.name: analyze_content
tools.description: Work on a tracked post, for analysis, as one of three kinds. breakdown (default) runs Break It Down: why it works, from the hook and structure to visuals, audio, the call to action, and steps to recreate it. scenes maps the post's scenes: each one's range, what happens and what is said in it; see a scene's frames with view. video downloads every video the post holds, its one video or each video slide of a carousel, into shared analysis copies, which the reading tools use; nothing lands in your library or counts against your storage. Once stored, each video answers with its cut list, where it changes scene, free. A post with no video says so: its images are already stored and readable. Sound is not analyzed on download: view the video with sound, or split it, to analyze its sound (free). Viewing an existing result is free; creating one spends credits (video is charged for what its downloads moved, holding the most they may move first), so pass getCost to see the price first. A breakdown or scenes still running returns pending: wait for it with get_status by the post's id (kind content for a breakdown, kind scenes for scenes), then call this again to read it at no charge. A video still downloading returns pending: call this again with the same kind to follow it, which is free.

contentId.description: The post: its id or short id, its link, or the platform's own id for it.

getCost.description: Return the credit cost instead of analyzing (nothing runs, nothing is charged). 0 when the result already exists, or for video when its copies are being made.

kind.description: breakdown (default): the Break It Down analysis. scenes: the scene map, each scene's range, what happens and what is said, priced per minute of video. video: every video the post holds in shared analysis copies, each with its cut list once stored, charged for what the downloads moved.

resolution.description: Only with kind video. The most detail the stored copy should have: the best the platform offers up to this is downloaded, charged for what arrives. A copy already at or above it costs nothing. Leave it out to keep the stored copy, or to get one at the standard detail.

tools.name: list_connected_accounts
tools.description: List the social accounts the owner has connected (the publish targets), default first. Use an account's id as connectedAccountId on a post in update_card, then publish_post. Read-only: connecting an account is done in the ContentHero app.

tools.name: get_connected_account
tools.description: Get one connected account's detail: platform, status, and capabilities. Use it to confirm a target can publish before attaching it to a post.

accountId.description: The connected account id from list_connected_accounts.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Get your ContentHero account: the credit balance, what is available to spend, credits reserved for work in progress, what was spent this month, the monthly spend cap, the plan and auto top-up. For a tracked social account, use get_tracked_account.

tools.name: update_account
tools.description: Update your ContentHero account. Only the fields you pass change. spendCap sets the monthly spend cap in credits, or null removes it: every credit spent this month counts toward it, and anything that would cross it is refused until the cap resets on the 1st of the month (UTC). Changing it needs the billing:write scope and the account's owner. Returns the account as it now is.

spendCap.description: The monthly spend cap in credits, or null for no cap.

tools.name: favorite
tools.description: Favorite or UNfavorite an asset: pass favorited:false to clear it (default true). For media (one output of a generation, an upload, stock), pass its mediaId as list_media, search_media and get_folder print it (a1B2c3D4-2 for one output of several). For anything else, pass assetType + id (card, voice, brand_kit, project, inspiration_content, gallery, transition, caption-template, template, space). Requires the favorites:write scope. Idempotent in both directions.

assetType.description: The kind of asset, for anything that is not media. Pass with id.

favorited.description: Default true. Pass false to UNfavorite.

mediaId.description: A media id, for media. A bare id for a generation with several outputs is refused with their media ids listed.

tools.name: archive
tools.description: Archive or UNarchive an asset: pass archived:false to restore it (default true). ContentHero never hard-deletes, so this is always reversible. For one output of a generation, pass its mediaId (a1B2c3D4-2 for one output of several). For anything else, pass assetType + id (card, brand_kit, brand_kit_section, project, space, template, style_library). Archiving is a timestamp and nothing else is touched, so a scheduled card restores as scheduled. Requires the favorites:write scope. Idempotent in both directions.

archived.description: Default true. Pass false to RESTORE (unarchive).

assetType.description: The kind of asset, for anything that is not media. Pass with id.

mediaId.description: A generated output's media id. A bare id for a generation with several outputs is refused with their media ids listed.

tools.name: share
tools.description: Make an item's public link, or stop sharing it with shared:false. Anyone with the link sees the item with no sign-in; a stopped link never opens again, and sharing again makes a new one. For media made in Studio, pass mediaIds: outputs of your finished generations, as list_media, search_media and get_folder print them. One output gives its generation's link, opened at that output; a generation keeps one link, so sharing it again returns the same page. Several give a new link to them as a set, leaving out any that cannot be shared. To stop a media link, name a generation by one media id or any media link as shareUrl. For anything else, pass assetType + id: a project's live link shows the project as it is now, a project has one link, and get_project reports it. An export's share page comes with get_export. Requires studio:write for media and editor:write for a project.

assetType.description: The kind of item, for anything that is not media. Pass with id.

mediaIds.description: For media: one or more media ids of outputs of your finished generations. To stop sharing, one.

shareUrl.description: For media, with shared:false: the media link to stop.

shared.description: Default true. Pass false to stop sharing.

title.description: For media: a title for a set of two or more.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the account's editor (video timeline) and canvas (slides/layers) projects. Filter by state (archived / favorited), by type (editor / canvas), or by a title search. Returns lightweight summaries; call get_project for a single project's full composition. Requires the editor:read scope.

filter.description: archived -> only archived; favorited -> favorited and not archived; omitted -> active (not archived).

type.description: Restrict to one project type; omitted returns both.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read a project: its title, revision and settings (its canvas size, and for a video project its frame rate, delivery loudness, magnetic main track, linkage and the kinds of track linkage reaches), with a summary of its composition by default or the whole composition with detail 'full'. The summary is each track's id, name, type, whether it is the main track and whether it is muted or hidden, and each clip's id, type, place on the timeline, speed, whether it is disabled and source: a clip plays a file (its assetId, the same id view and get_media take, and the window of the file it plays, in the file's seconds) or code (the project modules it imports). Clips that share an assetId were cut from one recording; a clip's id never says so. For a canvas, the summary is each slide with its layers' ids, types and the start of each text layer's text. A timeline read can be narrowed to a frame window or one track, and a canvas read to one slide; a narrowed full read carries only the modules its clips import and names the rest. A read that names clipIds, moduleNames, sourceAssetId or modulesIndex returns those parts alone: each clip named as its summary line, or whole with its code and the modules it imports with detail 'full'; each module named with its code; modulesIndex, every module's name, how many clips draw it, whether none does, and its size, without code; and with sourceAssetId and atSec, where moments of a recording play on the timeline: every clip and frame each second lands on, none where it was cut out. A read names parts or narrows the whole, not both. A project's read also lists the problems its code, modules and geometry hold, of the whole project or of the parts a read names: code reading what a project module does not provide, the compiler's warnings, modules no clip imports, and a zoom that shows a pinned region's own picture outside the pin. Pass the returned revision as expectedRevision on an edit, so a concurrent change to the same thing is refused rather than overwritten. update_project changes the settings. Requires the editor:read scope.

atSec.description: With sourceAssetId: the seconds of that recording to place.

clipIds.description: Read only these clips: each one's summary line, or whole with its code and the modules it imports with detail 'full'; nothing else of the project.

detail.description: 'summary' (default) returns the lightweight per-clip/per-layer structure; 'full' returns the complete composition with every property.

fromFrame.description: Timeline only: start of a frame window; returns clips overlapping [fromFrame, toFrame].

modulesIndex.description: Read the index of the project's modules: each one's name, how many clips draw it, whether none does, and its size, without code. Read alone, like the other parts.

slideId.description: Canvas only: scope the read to a single slide by id. Applies to detail:'full' as well. An id matching no slide returns every slide rather than nothing.

sourceAssetId.description: With atSec: the recording whose moments to place on the timeline, by the assetId a clip's source names.

toFrame.description: Timeline only: end of the frame window (see fromFrame).

trackId.description: Timeline only: scope the read to a single track by id.

tools.name: view
tools.description: See what the user is looking at, and see or hear your own work or a source. A view returns only what it names: your render, a source, or the user's screen; add live to a render to also get what the user is looking at. With nothing to render and no source, it returns the live context of the open app: the active surface, the focused element, the playhead and the selection, from the most recently active session, with the live participants. capture adds a picture of the user's screen as shown now, including unsaved and transient state; it takes a moment and briefly interrupts the page. render shows your work as it will play, rendered from the saved project: one composed frame or slide, the one in focus unless frame, slideId or slideIndex names another; for a timeline, frames, a count over a range, or perSecond over a range name several. count spreads that many frames from the first frame of the window to its last; perSecond steps from the first; frames and atSec are exact. Several frames come back one by one when they fit one result and otherwise as contact sheets with each frame labeled under its tile, in pages; nothing caps how many. width is the width of each image returned, the crop's when a region is named; without width a region comes back at native pixels. Each image names the frames it shows, sampled says how many were rendered, and anything the server changed is listed in adjusted with why. A contact sheet is a lossy, downscaled copy of its frames: use it to look, never to measure or to test whether two renders differ, because compression and scaling alter pixels that did not change. A difference found between sheets is not evidence of a difference between frames. trackIds and clipIds render only those tracks and clips, picture and sound, on the timeline's own frame numbers, leaving the project untouched, so the person can keep editing while you review. sound renders a range of the mix as an export mixes it, before an export's delivery leveling, and measures it (integrated loudness, true peak, loudness range, sample peak, where sounds start, stereo width, band balance), with a waveform and spectrogram picture and a link to the audio. Its sound is also analyzed and rendered as one evidence sheet, as a source's window is below, on the sound's own seconds from the start of the range; the measurement stays the loudness to deliver by. video watches a range play with its sound; where video cannot be received, as here, it returns frames across the range and the sound measured. To see and hear a source rather than your edit, name a clip of the user's with assetId (the id get_project reports in a clip's source) or mediaUrl, or a tracked post's video with contentId (and slide for a carousel) once analyze_content kind video has downloaded it, and window it with fromSec and toSec in its own seconds. A source's frames follow the same rules as your edit's, labeled with their seconds. A source read carries the source alone, and only the parts asked for. sound measures the window as it is, beside any frames; with video you watch it play. With sound, a stored source's window also carries its sound analysis for that window: speech, sound candidates with their measured descriptors, levels against the voice, offset from the beat and repetition pattern, music and beats, loudness, and each stem's level; made once per file, and made the first time its sound is read. The window also comes as one evidence sheet: its frames, the spoken words and a spectrogram strip per stem on one time axis, each sound candidate marked by its number. A candidate is measured, never named: judge what it is from its strip and its descriptors. find, where and picture ask a source, or a project's window over fromFrame and toFrame, of its picture analysis and answer in numbers rather than images, so a view with only them returns no frames. A file's picture analysis is made once and shared: a coarse one, one picture per shot, exists from upload, and the full one is made the first time the file is studied; until the full one is ready, the answer says it is coarse and how the full one stands. Every list in their answer comes a page at a time: limit sets how many of each list a page holds, and passing the answer's nextCursor back as cursor reads the next page of all of them. Anything not ready yet (a render's page, a sound analysis, an evidence sheet, a where) says when it started, when it is expected, the exact inputs that read it again (readWith, or the same inputs again when it names none), and why it has not ended when it is blocked or late. Read it again with exactly those inputs. A render that is not ready answers with a renderId: read it again with that id instead of rendering again. When rendering is busy the answer says how many seconds to wait before asking again. When the user is charged credits for what a view made, the answer says how many. Renders are ephemeral and need no live tab, only a projectId when no one is viewing. Check your work here, never with export, which makes a file the user keeps. Requires the context:read scope.

assetId.description: A clip of the user's to see and hear, by its asset id: the id get_project reports in a clip's source. Or pass mediaUrl or contentId.

atSec.description: Frames at exactly these seconds of a source, instead of spread across a window.

capture.description: Also return a picture of the user's screen as shown now, including unsaved and transient state. Use it only when the task depends on what the screen shows; to see your work, render it instead.

clipIds.description: Render only these clips, picture and sound, on the timeline's own frame numbers. The project is untouched.

contentId.description: A tracked post's video to see and hear, by its id or short id, its link, or the platform's own id for it, once analyze_content kind video has downloaded it. Or pass assetId or mediaUrl.

count.description: How many frames to spread from the first frame of the range, or of a source's window, to its last, both included. Omit for one frame at the focus point, or about one a second of a range.

cursor.description: Read the next page of every list of find, where or picture: pass the answer's nextCursor, with the same other inputs.

detector.description: The class of thing where answers from the file's own analysis instead of a phrase: a screen recording's pointer, or faces (where, never who). Leave find out. With track, a box you give is followed as that class.

find.description: Describe what to look for in the picture. Returns the moments of the source or project window that show it, best first, as times (and timeline frames for a project), matching what is pictured, the text on screen and the words spoken over it, each naming which of the three found it. The moments are candidates: confirm the ones that matter by viewing frames at their times, or ask where.

frame.description: Editor: which single timeline frame to render. Omit to render the current playhead frame.

frames.description: Editor: exactly these timeline frames, in this order.

fromFrame.description: Start timeline frame of the range, for several frames, sound or video. Omit to start at the beginning.

fromSec.description: Start of a source's window, in its own seconds. Omit to start at its beginning.

layout.description: 'frames' returns each frame as its own image; 'sheets' tiles them into contact sheets, an edit's frames numbered and a source's labeled with its second under each tile. Omit to choose by how many fit one result.

limit.description: How many items of each list a page of find, where or picture holds. Omit for the default.

live.description: Also return what the user is looking at beside a render.

mediaUrl.description: A clip of the user's to see and hear, by its media URL, rather than your edit. Or pass assetId or contentId.

page.description: Which page of the render, or of a source's frames, to read, starting at 1.

perSecond.description: How many frames to take per second of the range, or of a source's window, stepping from its first frame; never more than the footage has.

picture.description: The window's picture analysis: its cuts, fades, black, camera movement, the text on screen and where faces are (never who), each with its times and position. For a project it reads each clip's source and maps it to the timeline, and adds the edit's own cuts in editCuts: where a clip starts where the one before it ends without playing on from it. It does not see what covers a clip or what has no source, and names each clip it does not see with why; a render of the range shows those. Where a screen recording's pointer is, and its shape. To follow it to the exact frame, ask where with detector pointer and track the candidate.

projectId.description: The project to view or render. Omit for the surface the user is on now. Needed to render when no one is viewing.

region.description: Render only this rectangle, { x, y, width, height } in composition units (get_project's compositionSpace), to inspect detail. Without width it comes back at native pixels. For a source, the rectangle is in its own pixels.

render.description: Render your work from the saved project: one composed frame or slide, the one in focus unless frame, slideId or slideIndex names another, or the frames that frames, count or perSecond name. Frames across a range show motion, timing and pacing, finer the closer together they are.

renderId.description: Read a render already started, by its renderId, as a pending answer's readWith names it. Pass only page with it.

slide.description: Which video of a carousel post, by the slide analyze_content reports for it. Only with contentId.

slideId.description: Canvas: the id of the slide to render. Omit to render the focused slide.

slideIndex.description: Canvas: the 1-based slide index to render (alternative to slideId).

sound.description: Hear and measure sound: your edit's range mixed as an export mixes it, instead of its picture, by fromFrame and toFrame; or a source's window as it is, by fromSec and toSec, beside any frames asked for.

toFrame.description: End timeline frame of the range. Omit to run to the end.

toSec.description: End of a source's window, in its own seconds. Omit to run to its end.

track.description: Follow one thing on every frame of the window: a candidate's id from a where answer, or a time of the source and a box on its frame that you found yourself. Returns one track per stretch it is seen, its box on each frame as keyframes, and its edges where it appears and leaves. An edge is not always on the exact frame: view the frames either side before cutting on it. A thing without a firm outline is followed with a loose box, and very fast motion can end a track early or split it. Slower the first time a seed is asked, and a read after that.

trackIds.description: Render only these tracks, every clip on them, picture and sound, on the timeline's own frame numbers. The project is untouched.

video.description: Watch the range play with its sound, to judge motion, timing, transitions and pacing. Takes fromFrame and toFrame, or a source's window.

where.description: Also where on the frame each thing find describes may be: candidates, best first, each with an id, a confidence, its time span, its box normalized to the frame, what found it, and a time and box to check it on. View that frame to confirm the one you mean, then pass its id as track. When none is the thing, view the window's frames yourself, find it, and pass its time and box as track. Small things are found less often: check their candidates before trusting the first. Slower the first time a phrase is asked of a file, and a read after that.

width.description: The width in pixels of each image returned, the crop's when a region is named, to check legibility at the size it will be seen. Height follows the aspect ratio. Anything the server changed is listed in adjusted.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Addresses the words one of two ways. With projectId it reads the words as the timeline plays them, in timeline order. With mediaId it reads the words of that recording itself, within an optional window of the recording's own seconds, including spans no timeline plays. Pass exactly one. The window is start inclusive and end exclusive. A media read's times are in the recording's own clock, and its words come a page at a time with word granularity. The rest of this describes the project read. Read an EDITOR project's transcript mapped to its timeline clips, so you can do content-aware editing. Returns one segment per transcribable clip in timeline order, each carrying the words spoken within it plus its current state ([disabled] = cut/excluded from the render, [enabled] = kept) and its exact clipId. Use this to read what is said, see which parts are already disabled, then target the exact clipId(s) or source-time ranges with update_timeline (disable_ranges to non-destructively cut, set_disabled to toggle a whole clip). Pass `granularity: 'word'` to also get, per segment: word-level timing with ABSOLUTE timeline frames (so split / range ops are exact), per-word confidence + speaker, the derived silence gaps (for dead-air removal; already inset to the cuttable region so cutting them keeps breathing room), and the non-speech audio events; plus the distinct speaker set at the top level. In word mode each word, silence and audio event is a row of values in the order `fields` names. Segments come a page at a time in timeline order: pass the answer's nextCursor back as cursor for the next page, and limit sets how many a page holds. Scope it with `search` (a phrase to find) or `startMs`/`endMs` (a source-media window, which also clips the returned words) to read only the part that matters. Also returns the project's current `revision` so you can edit right away without a separate get_project: pass it as update_timeline's expectedRevision for a concurrency-safe edit, or omit expectedRevision to just apply to the current state. Returns mediaTranscribed:false when the media has not been transcribed yet. Requires the editor:read scope.

cursor.description: The answer's nextCursor, to read the next page of segments with the same other inputs.

endMs.description: Source-media end time in ms; companion to startMs.

endSeconds.description: With mediaId: where the window ends.

granularity.description: 'clip' (default) returns text per clip; 'word' adds word timing + absolute timeline frames + confidence + speaker, derived silences, and audio events.

limit.description: How many clip segments a page holds. Omit for the default.

mediaId.description: The recording whose words to read. Use instead of projectId.

paceThresholdMs.description: Word mode: minimum pause (ms) to report as a silence / dead-air region ("Pace"). Defaults to the project's saved pace, else 500.

paddingEndMs.description: Word mode: breathing room (ms) kept before speech at a silence end edge (negative tightens). Defaults to the saved padding, else 200.

paddingStartMs.description: Word mode: breathing room (ms) kept after speech at a silence start edge (negative tightens). Defaults to the saved padding, else 200.

projectId.description: The project whose timeline words to read. Use instead of mediaId.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring; returns only clip segments whose text contains it.

startMs.description: Source-media start time in ms; with endMs, returns only segments overlapping this window (and, in word mode, clips the returned words to it).

startSeconds.description: With mediaId: where in the recording the window begins, in the recording's seconds.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new project. `type` picks what it is: 'editor' (video timeline) or 'canvas' (slides/layers). All fields are optional; defaults match the in-app new-project flow (16:9 landscape, an editor project). A new canvas starts with one empty slide already, so add content to it with update_canvas create_layer (use create_slide only to add MORE slides); A new editor starts with one empty main track, named in the result: put the first clips on it with update_timeline create_clip, and add a track only for something that sits over the main story. When the project is for a planned piece, pass cardId to link it to that card in the same call. Returns the new project id + revision. Requires the editor:write scope (and planner:write with cardId).

cardId.description: The card this project is for: the new project is linked to it in the same call (it shows among the card's assets), so the card opens the edit from the moment it exists. Also needs the planner:write scope.

fps.description: Frames per second for an editor project: 24, 25, 30, 50 or 60. Defaults to 30.

height.description: Pixel height. Defaults from the orientation.

width.description: Pixel width. Defaults from the orientation.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export (render) a project's saved composition to a downloadable file the user KEEPS: a permanent deliverable that counts against the user's storage. To preview or verify a frame or slide while editing, do NOT export; use view with render (ephemeral, stored nowhere). The formats, what each makes and the options each takes are listed by get_schema kind 'export'; read it before choosing one. format 'mp4' works for both editor and canvas (a video render; may take a while). 'png' / 'jpg' work for both project types too: a canvas project renders one image per slide (multiple slides come back as a zip), while an editor project renders a single composited frame of the timeline (pick which frame with `frame`; defaults to frame 0). Canvas projects additionally support 'pdf' and 'pptx'. An editor project also exports its sound (mp3, aac, wav), its subtitles (srt, vtt) and its transcript (txt, docx, rtf, md, html). Resolution and watermark apply to every picture format: a free account never exports above 720p and never removes the watermark. `quality` is mp4 only. Returns the download URL when the export finishes in time, otherwise an exportId: wait for it with get_status (kind export), then read its file with get_export. Requires the editor:write scope.

format.description: Output format, one get_schema kind 'export' lists. Defaults to 'mp4'.

frame.description: Editor still (png/jpg) only: which timeline frame to render. Clamped to the composition length. Defaults 0. Use the playhead frame from view to render exactly the frame the user is viewing.

anyOf.description: A target integrated loudness, in LUFS. The server refuses one outside the range it accepts, and its refusal states that range.
Off: the mix plays and exports as it was mixed.

loudness.description: Rendered exports (video and sound) only: this export's loudness, in place of the project's own (get_project reads it). Omitted, the project's.

maxCharsPerLine.description: Subtitles (srt, vtt) only: the longest a line may be, 20 to 80 characters. Defaults 42.

maxLinesPerCard.description: Subtitles (srt, vtt) only: lines per subtitle card, 1 to 4. Defaults 2.

quality.description: mp4 ONLY: video bitrate. Meaningless for a still, which has no duration to spread bits over. Defaults recommended.

resolution.description: Output resolution, for EVERY format including stills. Defaults '720p' for an editor mp4 and the project's NATIVE size for a still or canvas mp4, in both cases clamped to your plan. 1080p and above are plan-gated: NAMING one above your plan is a 403, omitting one clamps instead.

showSpeakers.description: Subtitles (srt, vtt) only: name who speaks, when the captions hold more than one speaker. Defaults false.

timecodes.description: Transcripts (txt, docx, rtf, md, html) only: start each paragraph with its timecode.

watermark.description: Keep the watermark. Defaults true; removing it is plan-gated.

tools.name: list_exports
tools.description: List a project's exports, newest first, as the editor's Exports tab shows them: each finished one with its download and public share page, and the ones still running with their status (wait for one with get_status, kind export). A failed export is not listed. Requires the editor:read scope.

tools.name: get_export
tools.description: Read one export started by export: its file, state and details, with the download URL and public share page once it finishes. To wait for one still running, use get_status with kind export. Requires the editor:read scope.

exportId.description: The export id returned by export.

tools.name: delete_project
tools.description: PERMANENTLY delete a project. This is irreversible: the project, its edit history, and its render exports are destroyed (uploaded media stays in the library). To reversibly hide a project instead, use archive. You must pass confirm: true to proceed. Requires the editor:write scope.

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm the irreversible permanent delete.

projectId.description: The project id to permanently delete.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Change a project: its title, brand kit and cover, and its settings: canvas size, and for a video project its frame rate, delivery loudness, magnetic main track, linkage and the kinds of track linkage reaches. This is a PATCH: a field you omit is left alone. A setting belongs to the project and is shared by everyone who edits it; changing one is an edit, so undo_project_edit reverses it and every open editor shows it at once. To change what is in the composition, use update_timeline or update_canvas instead. get_project reads every setting. expectedRevision is the project revision you last read, and it means the same on update_project, update_timeline and update_canvas. An edit built on an older revision still applies when no change since touched what it touches. When one did, nothing is written and the answer is a conflict naming the current revision and what overlapped: read the project again and redo the edit. Omit it to apply to the project as it is. Returns the project with its settings as they now stand. Requires the editor:write scope.

brandKitId.description: A brand kit id from list_brand_kits, or null to clear it.

cover.description: How the cover is chosen: 'auto' follows the composition, { frame } is a chosen moment (for a canvas, a slide's index among its visible slides), { mediaId } is an image from the library.

coverPosition.description: Where the cover is framed, as percentages of its width and height, or null for the default framing.

expectedRevision.description: The project revision you last read, from get_project or the last edit. An older one still applies when nothing since touched what the edit touches; otherwise nothing is written and the conflict names the current revision and what overlapped. Omit to apply to the project as it is. On update_project it guards the settings in the document; the title, brand kit and cover are not versioned.

fps.description: Video projects only: the frame rate. Every frame number in the timeline converts with it, so clips keep their timing.

height.description: A pixel height, given with width.

linkage.description: Video projects only: whether clips on other tracks follow the main track's ripple and are deleted with the main clip they sit on.

linkedTracks.description: Video projects only: which kinds of track linkage reaches; a kind you omit is left alone.

anyOf.description: A target integrated loudness, in LUFS. The server refuses one outside the range it accepts, and its refusal states that range.
Off: the mix plays and exports as it was mixed.

loudness.description: Video projects only: the delivery loudness. Every export follows it.

magneticTrack.description: Video projects only: the magnetic main track. On, moving, trimming or deleting a clip on the main track closes the gap it leaves, and turning it on closes the gaps already there.

orientation.description: An aspect from the editor's list, or custom. Alone, it sets the size the editor gives that aspect.

width.description: A pixel width, given with height.

tools.name: update_timeline
tools.description: Edit a video timeline with a batch of operations, the same ones every ContentHero agent uses, applied by the server and shown in the open editor at once. Each operation is an object with an `op` name and its fields. get_schema kind 'timeline' lists every operation with its shape and the rules they all follow; read an operation in full by its name before using one you have not read, and build a clip from its type's example there. A code clip imports project modules, which an operation sets or copies from another of your projects. Read clip, track and transition ids from get_project. A batch is ordered and atomic: when any operation is refused, nothing is stored, and the result says which and why. The result reports each operation, with what the compiler found in any code an operation wrote, and what the edit left in the project that may not render as intended, clip by clip. Prefer an edit the person can review and turn back over one that cannot be reversed, and make a destructive one only when they asked for it. A clip's length on the timeline follows its source and its speed: change its speed, not its length. Project settings change with update_project. expectedRevision is the project revision you last read, and it means the same on update_project, update_timeline and update_canvas. An edit built on an older revision still applies when no change since touched what it touches. When one did, nothing is written and the answer is a conflict naming the current revision and what overlapped: read the project again and redo the edit. Omit it to apply to the project as it is. Every edit can be undone, and each returns the new revision. A retry that repeats the same operation id returns the revision already committed and never applies the batch twice. Requires the editor:write scope.

An older one still applies when nothing since touched what the edit touches; otherwise nothing is written and the conflict names the current revision and what overlapped. Omit to apply to the project as it is.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List the templates you can place: ContentHero's and the user's own (the editor's Elements panel), without their code, a page at a time. Each is code, a shape, an animated emoji or a logo, with its category, version and default size. Logos are listed only with kind logo, and search finds one by name or alias across the whole logo library. Place one with an insert_template op in update_timeline or update_canvas, branded with the project's brand kit; a logo's id is its slug; the logo library is a curated set kept in the product, so a brand's own logos are added through update_brand_kit; read one whole with get_template. Requires the editor:read scope.

Fields given beside a source override what it carries. Code is checked as it is written: code that does not compile is refused, with each finding's line and column. It is saved as made by you, and appears under My templates in the Elements panel. Requires the editor:write scope.

tools.name: list_style_libraries
tools.description: List the style libraries on this account. A style library is shared code that projects pin and import: components, design tokens, motion and sound cues, never a CSS style. Each entry gives its name, description, latest version and when it was last updated. Archived libraries are left out unless archived is true. Returns a page at a time; pass the answer's cursor for the next.

tools.name: get_style_library
tools.description: Read one style library by name: its description and every published version with its notes, newest first. With a version, read that version's modules instead, each by name with its code. A published version never changes. A project uses a library only after set_style_library pins a version in it.

tools.name: create_style_library
tools.description: Create a style library on this account, and publish its first version when modules are sent. A style library is shared code, not a CSS style. Its modules come from `modules` sent inline, from `fromProject` (modules of one project, read from its saved state, with imports between them rewritten to the library's own), or both; a name sent by both is refused. A library module may import the sandbox's modules and its own library's modules, never a project module. The name is fixed once created, because the code of every clip that imports the library names it. Publishing runs the same checks as saving a project module: code that does not compile, an import it cannot resolve, or a module that reads something another module does not provide is refused with the reason.

tools.name: update_style_library
tools.description: Publish the next version of a style library, edit its description, or both. A published version never changes: publishing adds one, and `notes` says what changed. Send modules inline (`code`, `edits` against `baseVersion`, or `null` to drop a module), from a project with `fromProject`, or both. A project that pins an earlier version is untouched until its own set_style_library moves it. Archive a style library with the archive tool, never by deleting: its versions are kept so every project that pins one still renders.
